ITEM G.1.
                             MEMORANDUM

TO:         Board of Trustees

THROUGH: Robert Harrison, District General Manager

FROM:       Kate Nelson, Director of Public Works

SUBJECT: (For Possible Action) Review and Approve Business Impact
         Statements Related to Ordinance No. 2 Rates, Rules, and
         Regulations for Sewer Service and Ordinance No. 4 Rates, Rules,
         and Regulations for Water Service by the Incline Village General
         Improvement District in Compliance with Nevada Revised Statute
         (NRS) 237.080. (Requesting Staff Member: Director of Public Works
         Kate Nelson)

DATE:       October 14, 2026



I.    RECOMMENDATION
That the Board of Trustees make a Motion to Approve the Business Impact
Statements Related to Ordinance No. 2 Sewer Service and Ordinance No. 4
Water Service by the Incline Village General Improvement District in Compliance
with Nevada Revised Statute (NRS) 237.080.

II.    BACKGROUND
The Incline Village General Improvement District (District) is considering approval
of updates to Ordinance No. 2 Sewer and Ordinance No. 4 Water, which
establish rates, rules, and regulations for sewer and water service. Because the
updates include changes to commercial service provisions and associated costs
to commercial businesses, NRS 237.080 requires the District to prepare a
Business Impact Statement for each ordinance and solicit input from affected
businesses prior to approval.

On September 16, 2026, the District distributed Business Impact Statement
notification letters to commercial sewer and water customers requesting
comments and supporting information regarding whether the proposed rate
adjustments would:
• Impose a direct and significant economic burden upon a business; or
• Directly restrict the formation, operation, or expansion of a business.

The comment period concluded on October 7, 2026, consistent with the statutory
requirement of at least fifteen (15) business days for responses. District staff
received two comments regarding the ordinances. All comments related to
difficulty locating or accessing the proposed amendments and did not identify
ivgid:2026-10-14:ivgid-agenda-packet:ee2.6:
concerns regarding potential economic impacts to businesses or restrictions on
the formation, operation, or expansion of a business. Staff provided information
to assist the commenters in locating the proposed amendments.

Based on the comments received and its review of the proposed amendments,
District staff prepared the Business Impact Statements pursuant to NRS 237.080
(Attachment 1). Approval of the Business Impact Statements fulfills statutory
requirements and allows the Board to proceed with consideration of the updates
to Ordinance No. 2 Sewer and Ordinance No. 4 Water.

III.  BID RESULTS
Not Applicable.

IV.    FINANCIAL IMPACT AND BUDGET
Approval of the Business Impact Statements does not authorize rate changes or
create a direct financial impact. This action satisfies the statutory procedural
requirements necessary for the Board to consider approval of the updates to
Ordinance No. 2 Sewer and Ordinance No. 4 Water.

V.     ALTERNATIVES
No alternatives are presented.

VI.    COMMENTS
The applicable Nevada Revised Statute for this Memorandum is NRS Chapter
318, including NRS 318.055, with the water and sewer powers granted pursuant
to NRS 318.116(11) and (15), NRS 318.140, and NRS 318.144, subject to the
applicable special-district formation requirements of NRS Chapter 308.

VII. BUSINESS IMPACT/BENEFIT
This item constitutes compliance with Nevada Revised Statutes Chapter 237
requirements. Approval of the Business Impact Statements allows the District to
proceed with consideration of the updates to Ordinance No. 2 Sewer and
Ordinance No. 4 Water in accordance with state law.

VIII. ATTACHMENTS
1.   IVGID 2026 Ord 2 and 4 BIS - Signed

                                 MEMORANDUM


TO:             Board of Trustees

THROUGH:        Robert Harrison
                District General Manager

FROM:           Heidi White
                District Clerk

SUBJECT:        PUBLIC HEARING – Time 4:00 P.M. and as soon thereafter as
                practicable.

                Public Hearing on the Proposed Amendments to Ordinance No. 2 –An
                Ordinance Establishing Rates, Rules, and Regulations for Sewer
                Services by Incline Village General Improvement District. No
                Adjustments to current Rates are Being Considered.

DATE:           October 14, 2026


On October 14, 2026, the Board of Trustees will hold a public hearing on the above
subject matter. Following is an outline for the public hearing:

1.    The Board Chair will ask the Board for a motion and a second to officially open the
      public hearing.
2.    Board Chair Tonking will call for the question, and the Board will take a vote to
      open the public hearing.
3.    Once the public hearing is open, the Board Chair will state that the District is
      holding a public hearing as required by the Nevada Revised Statutes.
4.    Board Chair Tonking will then ask either the Director of Public Works Kate Nelson
      or District General Manager Robert Harrison for the record, if the District complied
      with the required notice.
5.    Following confirmation, the Director of Public Works Kate Nelson will then provide
      an overview of the item and all of its components.
6.    Board Chair Tonking will state the Public Comments made during the public
      hearing are governed by the Chair, and Board. Chair Tonking should state the
      rules she wants to use.
7.    Board Chair Tonking will then ask for public comments on the proposed
      amendments as included in the Board packet.
8.    The duration of the public hearing is at the Board's discretion.
9.    After all public comments have been made, a Board member will need to make a
      motion to close the public hearing, which will need a second, and then the Board
      Chairperson will call for the question, and a vote will be taken on this motion.

THROUGH: Robert Harrison, District General Manager

FROM:       Kate Nelson, Director of Public Works

SUBJECT: (For Possible Action) Adopt Resolution No. 1930 - A Resolution
         Formally Approving the Amendments to Ordinance No. 2, an
         Ordinance Establishing Rates, Rules, and Regulations for Sewer
         Service by Incline Village General Improvement District. No
         Adjustments to Current Rates are Being Considered. (Requesting
         Staff Member: Director of Public Works Kate Nelson).

DATE:       October 14, 2026



I.    RECOMMENDATION
That the Board of Trustees make a Motion to Adopt Resolution No. 1930
Formally Approving Amendments to Ordinance No. 2, an Ordinance Establishing
Rates, Rules, and Regulations for Sewer Service by Incline Village General
Improvement District.

II.    BACKGROUND
The last comprehensive update to the Sewer Ordinance was approved by the
Board of Trustees on April 10, 2019. On July 30, 2025, a specific update to
Section 11.03 was also approved by the Board of Trustees (IVGID Ordinances |
Incline Village General Improvement District). The proposed amendments
(attached) are intended to provide administrative and technical updates to
improve the clarity, consistency, and applicability of the District Ordinance. The
revisions include cleanup of outdated language and provisions, updates to
maintain consistency with the District's current Standard Specifications for
Construction, and modifications to reflect current industry best practices.

In addition, the proposed amendments incorporate revisions necessary to
address applicable county code updates where appropriate. Collectively, these
updates are intended to improve the usability of the ordinances, eliminate
obsolete provisions, and ensure the District's regulatory framework remains
current while continuing to support the safe, reliable, and efficient operation of
the District's sewer systems.

III.  BID RESULTS
Not Applicable.

ITEM G.4.
                              MEMORANDUM

TO:         Board of Trustees

THROUGH: Robert Harrison, District General Manager

FROM:       Noemi Barter, Director of Finance

SUBJECT: (For Possible Action) Budget Transfer for payroll costs related to
         Parks employees from Internal Service Funds to Community Service
         Funds (Requesting Staff Member: Director of Finance Noemi Barter)

DATE:       October 14, 2026



I.     RECOMMENDATION
That the Board of Trustees approve the budget transfer from the Buildings
Internal Service fund to the Community Service fund, sub-fund Parks.

II.     BACKGROUND
With the fiscal year 2027 budget process and realignment of the organizational
structure with the building internal service fund and Parks, the Parks employees
were moved under the supervision of the Buildings Superintendent. Initially, the
finance department allocated the associated payroll costs related to the Parks
employees under the buildings internal service fund. However, after review of the
first two months of billing, time allocation and overall operations, parks activity
has been maintained as part of the facility fee and community services.
Therefore, to align with past and future practices the salaries, benefits and all
associated costs for Parks employees and activity will be transferred and remain
in the sub-fund 370 under Community Services Fund.

Per NRS 354.5980005, a local government need not file an augmented budget
for an enterprise or internal service fund with the department of taxation but shall
include the budget augmentation in the next quarterly report. To clarify further,
the proposed activity is not an augment/increase in budgeted amounts; this is
considered a transfer between enterprise funds and requires board action.

III.  BID RESULTS
There are no bidding requirements for this item.

IV.    FINANCIAL IMPACT AND BUDGET
The total financial impact is transferring a total of $263,420 in expenses in the
salaries and benefits categories from the Buildings Internal Service Fund to the
Community Services, sub-fund Parks and Beach Fund. Previous expenses
coded to buildings will be journaled to the correct organization and object code to

IVGID Board of Trustees                                          -12-                       Meeting Minutes September 9, 2026


          Item G.3. Presentation: Tahoe Meadows Potential All-Season Trailhead and
          Off-Highway Parking Presenter: Megan Kelly, District Manager, Nevada Tahoe
          Conservation District (NTCD) is available to be viewed/heard at:
          https://ivgid.portal.civicclerk.com/event/745/media
          Media Timestamp (00:58:10)

          Ms. Kelly provided an overview of NTCD’s mission, jurisdiction, and recent
          projects. She reported that NTCD received funding in 2025 from Washoe
          County and the Tahoe Fund to conduct a feasibility study for potential all-
          season, off-highway parking on SR-431 (Mt. Rose Highway) to address
          longstanding winter recreation issues, including trash, restroom access, and
          safety concerns. NTCD received letters of support for the study from IVGID,
          Nevada Nordic, NDOT, and the Snowlands Network.
          NTCD’s analysis identified the IVGID-owned five-acre parcel on the south side
          of Tahoe Meadows as the most viable non-federal option due to land
          characteristics and prior planning documents referencing it as a potential
          parking site. The parcel was acquired in 2008 using Nevada Question 1 Bond
          Program funds and is subject to a recorded deed restriction allowing recreation-
          related use. NTCD stated that a representative from the Nevada Department
          of Conservation and Natural Resources (DCNR) had informally indicated the
          parcel was “out of compliance” with the original grant purpose. This statement
          prompted concern and objection from the Board and legal counsel, noting that
          IVGID had received no formal notice and that such an assertion was
          inappropriate without official documentation.
          NTCD presented a conceptual design for a 50-space parking area including a
          bus pullout, restrooms, and trailhead kiosk, developed in coordination with
          NDOT, TTD, TRPA, and IVGID staff. Secondary options showed potential
          lower-parcel parking layouts and noted that any NDOT right-of-way concepts
          would be separate projects. NTCD also highlighted parallel efforts by the
          Nevada Division of Outdoor Recreation to develop a Tahoe Meadows Winter
          Safety Management Strategic Plan (expected November 2026), which NTCD
          intends to await before applying, its secured $150,000 Conserve Nevada grant
          toward design or permitting.

          IVGID Board members raised significant concerns including:

                    Accuracy and seriousness of the “non-compliance” statement, and its
                    inappropriate presentation without formal confirmation.

                    Mischaracterization within the feasibility study regarding a trustee’s
                    alleged support for east-side parking, which the trustee clarified was
                    incorrect and requested be removed.

ITEM I.3.
                             MEMORANDUM

TO:                Board of Trustees

THROUGH:           Robert Harrison, District General Manager

FROM:              Noemi Barter, Director of Finance

SUBJECT:           (For Possible Action) Award a Four-Year Bulk Fuel Purchase
                   and Delivery Agreement to Hunt Oil of California, in an
                   Amount Not to Exceed $190,000 per Year, Pursuant to NRS
                   332.065 and Board Policy 21.1.0, and Authorize the Closure
                   of the FY27 Blanket Purchase Order for Bulk Fuel with Flyers
                   Energy, LLC. (Requesting Staff Member: Director of Finance
                   Noemi Barter)

DATE:              October 14, 2026



I.     RECOMMENDATION
That the Board make a motion to award four year bulk fuel purchase and delivery
agreement to Hunt Oil of California, in an amount not to exceed $190,000 per
Year, Pursuant to NRS 332.065 and Board Policy 21.1.0, and Authorize the
Closure of the FY27 Blanket Purchase Order for Bulk Fuel with Flyers Energy,
LLC.

II.    BACKGROUND
On June 10, 2026, the Board of Trustees approved blanket purchase order
authority for Fiscal Year 2026-27, including $190,000 for the purchase and
delivery of bulk fuel from Flyers Energy, LLC. As of September 29, 2026,
$150,694.45 remains available under that authorization.

Following the Board’s approval, on July 1, 2026, Flyers Energy transitioned to
Diesel Direct West, LLC, which implemented changes to its delivery and
invoicing processes. Since the transition, District staff have experienced
extensive and ongoing administrative and billing issues, including delayed or
missing invoices, invoices associated with deliveries that could not be attributed
to the District, and invoices that did not identify the delivery location.

These issues have required significant staff time to research and reconcile fuel
purchases and have complicated the accurate allocation of fuel costs among
District operations. District staff repeatedly communicated these concerns to
Diesel Direct West in an effort to resolve the issues. Despite those efforts, the
problems have persisted and continue to create a significant administrative
burden.

TO:         Board of Trustees

THROUGH: Robert Harrison, District General Manager

FROM:       Noemi Barter, Director of Finance

SUBJECT: (For Possible Action) Authorization to Transact Under Blanket
         Purchase Orders for Fiscal Year 2026-27, Pursuant to NRS 332.15
         and Board Policy 21.1.0 (Requesting Staff Member Director of
         Finance Noemi Barter)

DATE:       June 10, 2026



I.     RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the Board of Trustees authorize the listed procurements
(blanket purchase orders) for FY2026-27 transactions in attachment A.

II.    BACKGROUND
Board Policy 21.1.0, Purchasing Policy for Goods and Services, adopted by the
Board of Trustees on February 14, 2024, requires that all contracts, including
purchase orders, for transactions expected to exceed $100,000 be approved by
the Board of Trustees. Board policy as well as NRS 332.115 further provides for
exceptions to the requirement for public advertising and competitive bidding for
specified contracts. The District’s Purchasing procedures require that a purchase
order is required for any contract or procurement exceeding $10,000. While
many Purchase Orders are tied to specific contracts or individually bid
procurements, Blanket Purchase Orders are used to cover multiple transactions
with a single vendor, typically for routine and recurring transactions.

In general, Purchase Orders or contracts exceeding $100,000 require Board
approval, provided that the underlying contract has been let consistent with the
public bidding requirements set forth in the NRS as well as the District’s
Purchasing Policy. However, NRS 332.115 (attached) provides for selected
exceptions to the public advertising and competitive bidding requirements.
Among the exemptions provided for in NRS 332.115 are purchases of goods and
commodities for resale at retail by public agencies. For the District, several
vendors utilized to supply food and beverage and golf merchandise for resale fall
within this exemption. This agenda item has been prepared seeking Board
approval for selected blanket purchase orders for planned procurement activities
with specific vendors, which are shown in attachment A.

SUBJECT: (For Possible Action) Approve the Jacks Valley Ranch Effluent

DATE:        October 14, 2026



I.    RECOMMENDATION
Approve the agreement with JVR Ranch.

II.    BACKGROUND
The District exports all treated wastewater effluent from the Lake Tahoe Basin
through its effluent export system, with the remaining flows ultimately conveyed
to the District’s wetlands facility in Carson Valley. Along the export pipeline, two
diversion structures allow treated effluent to be put to beneficial reuse prior to
reaching the wetlands facility.

One diversion serves the Clear Creek property, where approximately 115 acre-
feet of treated effluent has been diverted for irrigation of the golf course this year.
The second diversion serves the property historically known as Schneider
Ranch. Effluent has been available for irrigation of the Schneider Ranch property
intermittently since the 1970s. The property was subsequently acquired by Clear
Creek and later sold to the current owner, JVR Ranch. Over time, much of the
privately owned irrigation infrastructure serving the ranch deteriorated, resulting
in limited use of the effluent available through the diversion.

For the 2026 irrigation season, the District entered into a one-year purchase and
sale agreement with JVR Ranch for the use of treated effluent. The one-year
agreement provided JVR Ranch an opportunity to evaluate and improve the
existing irrigation infrastructure and determine the quantity of effluent that could
reasonably be put to beneficial agricultural use on the property.

With the one-year agreement concluding, JVR Ranch has requested a 30-year
agreement with the District for continued use of treated effluent for agricultural
irrigation. The proposed rate reflects the agricultural use of the effluent and is
therefore lower than the rate paid for the commercial irrigation use at Clear
